acceptance: sp_getapplock and sp_releaseapplock accept named (@Resource, @LockMode, @LockOwner, @LockTimeout, @DbPrincipal) and positional arguments, including EXEC @rc = ..., and return SQL Server's status codes (0 granted, 1 granted after wait, -1 timeout, -2 cancelled, -3 deadlock victim, -999 parameter/other error) with SQL Server's errors for invalid modes and owners.

Locks are shared across sessions of the same database with SQL Server's compatibility matrix for Shared, Update, IntentShared, IntentExclusive and Exclusive. Lock timeouts of 0, -1 (bounded by request cancellation) and N ms are honored. Session-owned locks persist until released or the session ends or resets. Transaction-owned locks require an open transaction and are released at the outermost commit or rollback. Locks are reference counted per owner.

APPLOCK_MODE and APPLOCK_TEST return SQL Server's values. Multi-connection tests cover contention, timeout, release, ownership and the generic repro EXEC sp_getapplock @Resource=N'foo', @LockMode='Exclusive', @LockOwner='Session', @LockTimeout=0.

tasks.title: Standing policy: resolve stale claims and reservations without owner approval
tasks.authorization: Direct owner instruction from mirek in this session (2026-10-01), issue #761, umbrella #710.
acceptance: The contributor instructions grant standing owner authorization for any session working on owner-approved work to resolve a stale claim or reservation that blocks it without asking: mark the stale task blocked and publish a bounded successor or companion task, recording the staleness evidence in the authorization.

Staleness is evidence-based (no pushes or PR updates to the task's branch for a stated period, no live local worker process or recently modified worktree, or a worker that reports itself stopped) and never applies to a live worker; the successor never reuses or deletes the old claim tag.

Sessions are told the owner is usually away for long periods and must keep progressing, reporting resolutions afterwards instead of asking; owner approval stays required only for real product decisions and external submissions.
